justification: Five files of evidence-page wording only (walk method box and the walking-test sentences); standard because the file count is over the minor limit, not because of logic.

pre_impl.existing_data: none: static component text and a pure function of the walk verdict
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If a test still asserts the old sentence it fails visibly in jest; no data is involved
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Every evidence page render uses the new sentences; nothing is stored

functions.name: walkWords
functions.input: the walk verdict object with kind, best walk and limit
functions.output: pill, sentence, margin and bottom-line strings for the walk
functions.if_none: a missing best walk keeps the existing 'walk is shorter than the limit' wording; only the verdict phrase changed

functions.name: WalkMethod
functions.input: the walk object from the evidence data
functions.output: the how-the-walk-is-calculated box with its numbered steps and text
functions.if_none: unchanged: optional fields are guarded as before

break_it.scenario: A verdict sentence changes in the function but a test or the page still shows the old one
break_it.what_happens: A reader sees 'meets the walking test' in one place and 'within the limit' in another
break_it.how: git grep for 'meets the walking' returns nothing; evidence-summary.test.ts asserts every verdict string

break_it.scenario: The route bullet claims the main walk only uses marked crossings
break_it.what_happens: A planner believes the headline walk already avoids unsignalled crossings
break_it.how: WalkMethod.tsx route bullet now says the route may cross wherever the map shows a crossing or junction and that the crossings-only walk is the restricted one

break_it.scenario: Straddle wording still says the lot meets the test
break_it.what_happens: A close-to-limit lot reads like a compliance finding
break_it.how: both straddle strings now say 'whether the walk is within the limit'; asserted in evidence-summary.test.ts:133,139

falsifiable_check.fails_when: any walk sentence differs from the text the tests assert, or the old 'meets the walking test' wording is rendered
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before the test strings were updated, evidence-summary.test.ts asserted 'On this measure the lot meets the walking test.' while the function now returns 'the walk is within the limit', which fails on string equality; after updating, 198 passed
